subject: Territory assurance matrix and ops checklist for residency commitments
messages:

Cc: Tom Blake <tom.blake@medcohealth.com>

Subject: Clarify: region guarantees & what temporary cross-region processing looks like

Hi Lauren / Karthik,

Thanks for the call earlier — a couple follow-ups from our security and privacy team so we can close open items for procurement: 

1) Residency guarantee: Can you confirm the SLA for keeping EU customer data in EU regions (at rest and in transit) and what windows are tolerated for temporary cross-region processing during failover? We need the explicit maximum window documented.
2) Subprocessors: We need the most recent roster and onboarding dates for any cloud infra subprocessors that may see decrypted data (KMS/HSM operators excluded).
3) KMS / key control: If we bring our own key (BYOK), does Redwood execute any operations that would cause key material to leave the EU? Please confirm key wrapping/transport behavior.
4) DPA redlines: Our legal team will send suggested edits — can you provide a point person to negotiate the DPA addendum and a rough turnaround time?

We want to map these answers into our internal decision matrix this week. Would appreciate a short matrix or checklist we can slot into the review.

Thanks,
Sabrina
Sabrina Wu
Sr. Information Security Manager, MedCo Health

Subject: Re: Clarify: region guarantees & what temporary cross-region processing looks like

Hi Sabrina — thanks for the clear list. Sending a concise package to answer each point below and attached a working matrix + our current DPA redline. Short answers first, details in attachments:

1) Residency SLA: For EU region-anchored contracts we commit to regional processing for production traffic with a documented transient failover window up to 72 hours in extreme infrastructure disruption (this is our operational maximum; typical failovers are < 3 hours). See 'territory_assurance_matrix_v1.xlsx' for operational triggers and escalation timelines.

2) Subprocessors: Attached is the up-to-date roster (subprocessor_roster_2026-02-17.csv) that lists subprocessors and activation dates. Per policy, subprocessors that process decrypted customer payloads are limited and noted in the roster; we flag those rows with a "payload_access" column.

3) KMS/BYOK: We support customer-managed keys. With BYOK the key material never leaves customer-managed KMS/HSM in the region; Redwood uses ephemeral wrapping keys for transport but we do not persist customer key material. See the KMS note in the matrix.

4) DPA redlines: Looping Marissa (Legal) — Marissa will be lead on negotiations. Typical turnaround for an initial DPA counter is 3 business days after receipt of your redlines, faster if it's limited scope.

Next steps:
- Marissa will review your legal points and propose a path for signature.
- Monica will provide operational evidence links and confirm telemetry for audit logs (S3 presigned streams/audit-log retention).
- Karthik will outline the failover steps, replication guarantees, and a short ops checklist for your SOC.

I attached: DPA_v2_redlined.pdf (initial counter), territory_assurance_matrix_v1.xlsx, subprocessor_roster_2026-02-17.csv

Happy to jump on a 30-min sync if you'd like to walk through the matrix.

Best,

Hi Sabrina — I'm Marissa on Redwood Legal. Thanks for the questions; quick legal summary here while we review any redlines you send: 

- DPA: We generally accept region-anchoring commitments in a DPA addendum; any exceptions or carve-outs are surfaced explicitly. We can accommodate a clause that requires notice and windows for allowed temporary cross-border processing (we'd look to mirror the operational 72-hour max Lauren noted).
- Subprocessors: We'll provide an SOC2-style subprocessor attestation and the roster. If you need contractual novation or direct flow-downs for certain subprocessors, flag those vendors and we'll triage.
- Audit evidence: We can provide audit log exports and a telemetry package for a one-time review; ongoing retention beyond standard terms can be discussed as an add-on.

Please send the redlines when ready — I'm the primary negotiator and aim to turn around contractual comments within 3 business days. If there's a narrow set of legal asks (e.g., stricter failover window, specific audit retention period), note them in a short doc so we can scope internally.

Regards,

Hi Sabrina — Karthik from Ops/Infra here. A few operational clarifications you can drop into your decision matrix: 

- Failover behavior: During a region outage we fail requests over to the configured secondary region. For pinned accounts you can opt for "strict" pinning (no automatic cross-region route) or "pinned-with-failover" (automatic cross-region route with 72h telemetry window). By default, enterprise contracts use "pinned-with-failover" unless strict pinning is requested and an ops carve-out is agreed.

- Data in transit & at rest: All inter-region replication uses TLS 1.3 with additional transport-layer encryption. At-rest replication between regions is encrypted with service-managed keys unless BYOK is selected. If you choose BYOK and host the key in your EU KMS, Redwood will never store key material; wrapped keys used for ephemeral bootstrap are not retained.

- KV cache / inference state: Model KV caches are not exported outside the region for strict pin customers; for pinned-with-failover we snapshot and replicate only the minimum metadata needed to resume sessions and we mark those artifacts for deletion after the failover window.

- Evidence & telemetry: I uploaded an evidence bundle to the shared Drive folder (link in earlier email). For your SOC review I can provide a sanitized set of audit logs and a step-by-step of the failover runbook.

Operational ask: if you need a shorter failover maximum (e.g., 24 hours), we'll need to scope additional standby capacity and a playbook change; we can provide a cost estimate for that option.

Happy to demo the failover sequence in a 20-min session — propose Thu 19 Feb 14:00 PT if that works for you.

-Karthik
